report_name: Microsoft's 'agent-framework' PyPI Package Hijacked to Steal Credentials

threat_actors.name: Unnamed Threat Actor
threat_actors.description: An unidentified threat actor who executed a supply chain attack by compromising Microsoft's official 'agent-framework' package on the Python Package Index (PyPI). The actor published malicious versions to steal developer and CI/CD credentials for various cloud and development platforms.
threat_actors.goals: To harvest secrets from developer environments and CI/CD pipelines to gain unauthorized access to cloud infrastructure and software development workflows.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor compromised the software supply chain by gaining publishing rights to the official Microsoft 'agent-framework' project on PyPI and distributing malicious versions (1.26.1 and 1.26.2).

attack_patterns.name: Trusted Relationship
attack_patterns.description: The attack exploited the implicit trust developers have in the official Python Package Index (PyPI) and in packages published by a reputable vendor like Microsoft.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Python
attack_patterns.description: The credential-stealing payload was written in Python and executed within the Python interpreter environment after being installed via a malicious package.

attack_patterns.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
attack_patterns.description: A malicious .pth file was used to automatically execute the credential-stealing code upon Python interpreter startup, a mechanism analogous to startup folder persistence in the Python ecosystem.

attack_patterns.name: Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
attack_patterns.description: The malware searched for and parsed credentials from developer configuration files such as `~/.docker/config.json` and `~/.npmrc`.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Application Access Token
attack_patterns.description: The malware actively attempted to generate and steal Azure managed identity tokens, Azure DevOps OIDC tokens, and GitHub Actions OIDC tokens to impersonate CI/CD workflows and access cloud resources.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The attackers potentially used compromised developer credentials to gain publishing access to the PyPI project, although the exact method of access is unknown.

malware.name: agent-framework credential stealer
malware.description: A credential-stealing payload embedded in malicious versions (1.26.1, 1.26.2) of the 'agent-framework' PyPI package. It executes automatically on Python interpreter startup via a .pth hook to harvest secrets for Azure, AWS, GitHub, Docker, and npm from environment variables and configuration files.

identities.name: Python Package Index (PyPI)
identities.description: The open-source software registry that was used to distribute the malicious package versions.

identities.name: Azure
identities.description: Cloud platform targeted for credential theft by the malware, including managed identity and DevOps OIDC tokens.

identities.name: AWS
identities.description: Cloud platform targeted for credential theft by the malware.

identities.name: GitHub
identities.description: Software development platform targeted for credential and OIDC token theft.

identities.name: Docker
identities.description: Container platform targeted for credential theft from its configuration file (~/.docker/config.json).

identities.name: npm
identities.description: Package manager targeted for credential theft from its configuration file (~/.npmrc).

identities.name: Hugging Face
identities.description: AI platform targeted for credential theft from its configuration files.

infrastructure.name: agent-framework PyPI Project
infrastructure.description: The official Microsoft 'agent-framework' project on the Python Package Index (PyPI) that was hijacked by threat actors to publish and distribute malicious versions containing a credential stealer.

indicators.name: Suspicious Python Startup Hook Creation (.pth file)
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Python Startup Hook Creation (.pth file)
id: 0c8a3d1e-5f6b-4a9c-8d1e-2f3a4b5c6d7e
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of .pth files in Python site-packages directories. These files can execute code on interpreter startup and were used for persistence in the agent-framework supply chain attack.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/microsofts-agent-framework-pypi-package-compromised-to-steal-credentials/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-19
tags:
  - attack.t1547.001
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains: 'site-packages'
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.pth'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of .pth files in Python site-packages directories, a technique used for persistence by the malicious 'agent-framework' package.

indicators.name: Python Accessing Sensitive Credential Files
indicators.pattern:
title: Python Accessing Sensitive Credential Files
id: 1d9b4e2f-6a7c-4b8d-9e2f-3a4b5c6d7e8f
status: experimental
description: Detects a Python interpreter process accessing common developer credential files. This behavior was exhibited by the malicious 'agent-framework' package to steal secrets.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/microsofts-agent-framework-pypi-package-compromised-to-steal-credentials/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-19
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\python3.exe'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
  selection_files:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '.docker\config.json'
      - '.npmrc'
      - '.aws\credentials'
      - '.huggingface\'
      - '/.docker/config.json'
      - '/.npmrc'
      - '/.aws/credentials'
      - '/.huggingface/'
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects a Python process accessing common developer credential files, a key behavior of the 'agent-framework' credential stealer.

indicators.name: Python Accessing Cloud Metadata Service
indicators.pattern:
title: Python Accessing Cloud Metadata Service
id: 2e0c5f3a-7b8d-4c9e-8f3a-4b5c6d7e8f9a
status: experimental
description: Detects a Python interpreter process making a network connection to the cloud instance metadata service (169.254.169.254). This technique was used by the malicious 'agent-framework' package to steal instance tokens.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/microsofts-agent-framework-pypi-package-compromised-to-steal-credentials/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-19
tags:
  - attack.t1528
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
detection:
  selection_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\python3.exe'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
  selection_network:
    DestinationIp: '169.254.169.254'
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects a Python process making a network connection to the cloud instance metadata service, a method used by the malware to steal Azure managed identity tokens.
